answer: Data-grounded hypothesis: **Interviews are the most commonly used technique for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects.** Among the 194 respondents who answered the elicitation-technique question (Q9), 97 reported using interviews — 50.000% (95% percentile bootstrap CI [42.784, 57.216]) — the highest share across all six listed techniques (Scenarios 38.660%, Prototyping 38.660%, Workshops/Meetings 38.144%, Observation 32.990%, Others 5.670%). Interviews also rank first under the all-276 denominator at 35.145%. The stated claim figure of 69.399% (95% CI [69.062, 69.735]) is NOT reproducible from the supplied file: no single-technique use rate comes close (the maximum is 50.0% for Interviews), and the claimed CI's width implies a binomial sample of roughly n≈72,000 versus the n=276 in this dataset. The supplied CSV evidently replaced the original numeric answer grades with `quoted`/`not quoted` tokens (a survey-export artifact), so the 69.4% figure likely came from an earlier, undamaged analysis. On the data actually provided, the most commonly used elicitation technique is Interviews at ~50.0% of valid respondents (not 69.4%), and this remains the answer with the stated uncertainty about the claim's provenance.

payload.hypothesis: Interviews are the most commonly used technique for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects (97/194 valid respondents = 50.000%, 95% bootstrap CI [42.784, 57.216]), the highest of the six Q9 techniques. The stated 69.399% (95% CI [69.062, 69.735]) figure is not reproducible from the supplied data.
payload.workflow: 1) Read CSV as strings; Q9_ML_Elicitation_* columns contain only {'quoted','not quoted','-77'}. 2) Validated encoding via cross-tabulation with Q9_ML_Elicitation_Others_Free: 'quoted'=technique selected (free text present), 'not quoted'=not selected, '-77' (paired with '-66' in free-text col) = question not answered/NA; the same 82 rows carry '-77' across all six Q9 columns (valid n=194 of 276). 3) Primary statistic: %use = 100*count(selected)/194 per technique; robustness: /276 with -77 as not selected. 4) 'Most commonly used' = max %use -> Interviews (50.000%). 5) Bootstrap: resample with replacement from each technique's 0/1 selected vector among the 194 valid responders, B=10,000 replicates, seed=42, percentile method (2.5/97.5); CIs computed per technique. 6) Claim check: 69.399% lies outside every computed CI; max achievable single-technique rate is 50.000%; claimed CI width implies n~72,049, inconsistent with n=276 — reported as a data limitation, not force-fit.
